page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, with 2 threads per core operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The CPU features a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, featuring a 2500 GB NVMe SSD, while network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2314.0 placing it in the top tier. Single-threaded tasks perform well, as demonstrated by a strong gzip compression rate of 34.74 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.0 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show some limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated as weak at 4390.57, and memory read-only bandwidth for large blocks is also weak at 34.18 GB/sec. Despite these multi-threaded constraints, database and transactional operations remain stable, with Redis SET operations achieving an average of 6.09 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 3266.21.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7ie.xlarge offers high resource density by combining a substantial 2500 GB local NVMe SSD with 32.0 GB of DDR5 RAM on a 4-vCPU footprint. This hardware profile is optimized for storage-heavy and memory-intensive workloads rather than raw multi-core compute power. The instance is well-suited for relational databases, NoSQL transactional stores, caching layers like Redis, and moderate web serving applications that require fast local storage access and high single-core performance.
